chapter_theme: The light of grace (அருள் ஒளி): those who stand in grace are freed of the bonds, and the poet tells how, seeking with song and tears, he was given Siva's feet, made spotless and fed nectar. Grace is a lamp that turns its bearer into light, and when light and darkness both pass the soul becomes Siva.
structure_note: A verse on standing in grace (1814) is followed by first-person testimony of what Nandi gave (1815 to 1817, 1820), verses on the lamp and the light (1818, 1819), and two closing verses on grace as refuge (1821) and a challenge about birth and death (1822).

1814.reading: Those who stand first in grace know and do not sink; those who do not stand in grace do not leave the five bonds, know not grace's greatness and do not draw near; born in grace, they know by knowing.
1814.nuance: ஐம்பாசம் (the five bonds) is traditionally anava, karma, maya, mayeya and the concealing power; the verse does not list them. Who is 'born in grace' in line 4 is unclear: perhaps those of line 1, perhaps everyone, as in 1800.

1815.reading: Great Nandi gave the way of no return; Nandi the blissful gave nectar that never sates; the Lord of a thousand names said, in a single name, 'Bathe in the insatiable sea of grace.'
1815.nuance: வாரா வழி, the road from which one does not come back, is release from rebirth. பேர் ஒன்றினில் may mean 'by one of his names' or that the thousand names are summed in one, which tradition may take as the five-letter mantra.

1816.reading: Dancing, singing, weeping and crying out, seeking, I found Siva's great nature; as he joined me he gave me a sign that is no sign and stood within me, and I gained his grace.
1816.nuance: The first line is the vocabulary of ecstatic devotion. குறியாக் குறி, 'a sign that is not a sign', is traditionally the Lord beyond form given in a form, or the guru's teaching; the verse leaves it open.

1817.reading: Treating the birth I came into and the impurity that came with it as a film of maya I had clung to, I set my feet on your way saying 'you are my father', great Nandi; I left what I had learned and bowed at your anklet.
1817.nuance: அத்தனை நீயென்று may be 'you are the father' (அத்தன்) or 'you are all that' (அத்தனை); அடிவைத்தேன் may be 'I stepped forward' or 'I placed myself at your feet'. கற்றன விட்டேன் is a strong phrase: learning is put down, not completed.

1818.reading: Light the lamp and know the open space; before the lamp suffering changes; those who hold the lamp that lights the lamp become themselves the lamp that shines in the lamp.
1818.nuance: விளக்கு (lamp) occurs in every line, and விளக்கும் also means 'explains' or 'makes clear'. வெளி (open space) may be the yogic inner sky. Tradition reads the lamp that lights the lamp as grace or the guru kindling knowledge.

1819.reading: Light and darkness never end once and for all; only for those in the light does the light not fail; light and darkness are as different as an eye that has seen them; when both light and darkness go, the soul becomes Siva.
1819.nuance: Line 3 is obscure. The last line goes past the usual image: release is not light defeating darkness but both passing, which tradition may read as going beyond knowledge and ignorance alike.

1820.reading: Me, who wandered outside, he crowned with his golden anklets, entered my very nature and made me spotless, entered as dharma and gave me nectar; I sat dazed, wondering how he did it.
1820.nuance: பொற்கழல் சூட்டி, crowning with the anklets, is placing the feet on the head, the gesture tradition calls திருவடி தீட்சை. நிறமே may be 'my colour' or 'my very being'.

1821.reading: There is one wide place called grace and one refuge called the true thing; when the one who entered the mind to remove delusion is grasped with clarity, the way to Siva follows.
1821.nuance: மருள் (delusion) and தெருள் (clarity) are paired. Grace and the true thing may be two names of one refuge or two stages, grace leading to the real.

1822.reading: Tell us how you were born before and died here; another god's version of the truth is set aside; casting off the body that vultures adorn, we shall clothe the precious soul in clarity: can you say this?
1822.nuance: The verse reads as a challenge to those who cannot account for their own births and deaths. Line 2 (வேறொரு தெய்வத்தின் மெய்ப்பொருள் நீக்கிடும்) and தேறுஅணிவோம் are obscure, and the reading is a guess.

links.note: The Kural asks what learning has achieved if it does not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge, so bowing is learning's fruit. Tirumular bows by leaving what he learned (கற்றன விட்டேன்): the feet are reached by setting learning down.
Both set a true lamp above ordinary lamps. For the Kural it is truthfulness; for Tirumular it is the lamp that lights the lamp, and its bearer becomes the lamp.

source_issues: 1819 line 3: ஒளியுருள் may be a misprint for ஒளியிருள்; the line is obscure.
1822 lines 2 and 4 (மெய்ப்பொருள் நீக்கிடும், தேறுஅணிவோம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
